title: Toggle a touchpad's mouse-emulation sibling with it
head: 7df997857916
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The updated executable lost its execute bit, so checkout and dev-linked touchpad/touchscreen toggles fail before running
leads.consequence: Both bin/omarchy-toggle-touchpad and bin/omarchy-toggle-touchscreen exec the helper by command name. In a checkout or omarchy dev link, invoking either returns permission denied (exit 126), without changing the device, saved state or OSD. The new shell test also exits 126 at its first toggle, before any of its new assertions run. Restore executable mode for bin/omarchy-toggle-input-device; the test script itself also changed from 100755 to 100644, although test/shell invokes tests via bash and is not blocked by that mode change. Important qualification: the external omarchy package PKGBUILD uses install -Dm755 for every bin/*, so installed /usr/bin binaries regain execute permission; this issue directly affects checkout/dev-link operation and tests, not necessarily packaged production installations.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N-MODE; verified by coordinator git ls-tree; published

leads.summary: Open touchpad natural-scroll PR #6916 checks the old disabled.lua state path; if merged together, its Enabled checkmark never turns off
leads.location: #6916 default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc, trigger.hardware.touchpad.enabled (diff hunk @@ -69,+69); current PR bin/omarchy-toggle-input-device:29,96,117
leads.consequence: The #6916 description explicitly intends a live Enabled checkmark. Its check is [[ ! -f $HOME/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/touchpad-disabled.lua ]]. This PR stores disables in touchpad-disabled-name, and migration removes touchpad-disabled.lua, so after off the added menu child still shows 'Enabled ✓'. Clicking it toggles on, but the displayed mark does not reflect the state on either side. Change the other PR's check to ! -f .../touchpad-disabled-name during integration. The two PR heads are diverged, not stacked. The #6916 patch dry-runs and applies to a private copy of this head's menu with offset five and no rejects/conflict markers; GitHub currently returns UNKNOWN for #6916 mergeable, so this is a demonstrated combined-code consequence, not a claim of GitHub mergeability. This PR's existing fixture does not assert the other PR's menu guard.
leads.triage: dropped: open #6916 checks touchpad-disabled.lua but base already uses touchpad-disabled-name (base/bin/omarchy-toggle-input-device:28); pre-existing mismatch not caused by #12360

leads.summary: The end-user toggle manual still describes saving only one device and does not disclose the pointing-stick side effect
leads.consequence: The script header now describes toggling both device names and the pointing-stick caveat, but the user-facing manual says 'the disabled device's name is saved' and 'disable it again' without noting that turning off a touchpad may also disable its -mouse node and hence a sharing pointing stick until on. Users who rely on a pointing stick or inspect the name file cannot infer this effect from the manual. Amend the Touchpad paragraph in manual/13-toggles-idle-screensaver.md:24 to state that a compatible -mouse sibling is also disabled and persisted and mention the shared pointing-stick possibility. The PR description is not a substitute for the published manual.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus optional manual note; verified manual line 24; published as Documentation note

limits: Did not run hardware or a live compositor; no physical input devices are assigned. Shipped Hyprland v0.56.2 code confirms mice JSON and pointer disabled semantics, but Linux HID/libinput's physical node relationships were not independently established here. Therefore the pointing-stick behaviour is reported as a documentation parity problem grounded in this PR's explicit caveat, not independently verified on hardware.

flags.claim: If that first query fails, which is what happens when the compositor briefly does not answer, ...
flags.why: My evidence only shows what happens when the first (detection) query fails (probes B2/B4). Nothing shows that a brief compositor outage hits the first query rather than the second; the fixed case (second query fails, probes A2/B3) is also a brief-outage case. 'which is what happens' presents one outcome of a transient failure as the outcome.

The first-query-failure result in the Notes (and the dev-link W cases) used the real `omarchy-hw-touchpad` from the pinned tree with a stubbed `hyprctl` (probes B1-B8, W1-W4 have hw=real in results.jsonl). The Notes' point depends on that script being real, so saying it was stubbed contradicts the note above it.

flags.claim: Together they show that both kinds of `Mouse` node exist and that udev cannot tell them apart.
flags.why: c4f072aaaded sets ID_INPUT_POINTINGSTICK=0 for every i2c `*Mouse` name (hwdb.d/60-input-id.hwdb:61-63, v262 and main), and systemd issue #36677 says heuristics would be needed. That shows udev's current rules do not separate them, not that it cannot. The script header also says 'does not separate them'.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed to 'current rules do not separate them'

flags.claim: the package build installs every `bin/*` with mode 755.
flags.why: omarchy PKGBUILD:115-126 (omacom/omarchy-pkgs master) skips omarchy-debug, omarchy-debug-idle and omarchy-upload-log, which ship from omarchy-settings (not checked). For this script the claim holds; 'every' is slightly too broad. Nitpick.

Correct per probe B8 (step 2 `on` enables both). Dropped from my evidence: with the toggle key, which is the default binding (media.lua:13), the next press disables again because the saved file is gone, so it takes two presses (probe B7 step 2 shows OSD 'Touchpad disabled', step 3 enables). A reader may assume pressing the toggle key again recovers.

flags.claim: Suggested change: `git update-index --chmod=+x bin/omarchy-toggle-input-device` (and the test file, to match the base).
flags.why: update-index changes only the index; the author's working-tree file stays 644, so with core.fileMode=true `git status` keeps showing a mode change and a later `git commit -a`/`git add -A` would revert the fix, and their local test run still fails. Adding `chmod +x` covers both cases.
flags.disposition: real gap, suggestion now includes chmod +x

flags.claim: 'The reasoning in the reply holds up, so neither point is raised again here.' vs the Documentation note suggesting the manual carry the pointing-stick caveat.
flags.why: The documentation note does return to the pointing-stick point, albeit as a manual suggestion. Nitpick; either soften line 7 ('neither behavior is questioned again') or leave.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12360#issuecomment-5832592293) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12360#issuecomment-5842692101), checked at `7df99785`.

**Verified:** `on` now restores the names `off` saved, so the stuck-sibling case from the earlier review is resolved. The header comments now describe the multi-name file. The pointing-stick side effect and the `off` fallback are kept on purpose and documented in the script header. The reasoning in the reply holds up, so neither is raised again as a finding here. One new issue: the commit drops the executable bit from the toggle script.

| Earlier point | Status at `7df99785` |
|---|---|
| `on` rediscovers the sibling instead of using the saved names | Resolved |
| Header comments describe a single saved name | Resolved |
| `-mouse` match can also disable a pointing stick | Kept on purpose, documented in the script header |
| `off` with a failed sibling lookup saves only the touchpad; `on` enables a user-disabled `-mouse` node | Kept on purpose |

### `bin/omarchy-toggle-input-device` lost its executable bit

Commit `7df99785` changes the script's Git mode from `100755` to `100644`. The GitHub diff shows `old mode 100755 / new mode 100644`. The test file changed the same way, which is harmless because `test/shell` runs tests with `bash`.

```text
omarchy-toggle-touchpad / omarchy-toggle-touchscreen
  -> exec omarchy-toggle-input-device        (mode 644 in a checkout)
       only copy on PATH        -> Permission denied, exit 126
       packaged copy later on PATH -> bash skips the 644 file and runs the packaged copy
```

- `test/shell.d/toggle-input-device-test.sh` on a clean head checkout stops at its first toggle (`Permission denied`, exit 126). With only the mode restored, all 19 checks pass.
- In `omarchy dev link` mode the checkout's `bin` comes first on PATH. In a stubbed run with an executable copy later on PATH, the later copy ran, so only the touchpad was disabled and none of this branch's code ran.
- Packaged installs are not affected: the package build installs this script with mode 755.

**Impact:** from a checkout, the touchpad and touchscreen toggles (keys and menu) either fail outright or silently run the old packaged script, and the repository test fails.

**Suggested change:** `chmod +x bin/omarchy-toggle-input-device && git update-index --chmod=+x bin/omarchy-toggle-input-device` (and the same for the test file, to match the base). Updating only the index leaves the working-tree file at 644, so a later `git commit -a` would revert the fix.

### Notes

**Optional:** the new saved-name restore runs only after `require_device`. The real `omarchy-hw-touchpad` calls `hyprctl devices -j` itself. If that first query fails (for example when the compositor briefly does not answer), `on` exits 1 with `No touchpad device found`, deletes the saved file and re-enables neither node. The touchpad side of this matches the earlier head and the base, and a second `on` recovers. With the default toggle key it takes two more presses, since the next press sees no saved file and disables again. The new test stubs `omarchy-hw-touchpad`, so it only covers a failure of the second query. In a stubbed run, applying the saved names before `require_device` restored both nodes in this case and still passed the full test file.

**Documentation note:** `manual/13-toggles-idle-screensaver.md:24` still says "the disabled device's name is saved". It could mention the `-mouse` sibling and the pointing-stick caveat that the script header now carries.

**Correction to the earlier review:** kernel commit [40d5bb87377a](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/40d5bb87377a599d0405af765290f28aaa6abb1e) was cited as support for the pointing-stick case. It actually says the trackstick's events were *ignored* in the merged node, because the emulation collection had already mapped X/Y and the buttons. The better sources are systemd commits [3d7ac1c655ec](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/3d7ac1c655ec40f3829543072494dcdfb92dbc6b) ("The built-in trackpoint, if any, is then the i2c mouse device") and [c4f072aaaded](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/c4f072aaadedd9029bf0bef2036fdab8a4a3c180) ("Many i2c touchpads get a '... Mouse' event node which is mislabelled as pointingstick"). Together they show that both kinds of `Mouse` node exist and that udev's current rules do not separate them. That matches the caveat now in the script header.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the new commit and its callers, plus Hyprland v0.56.2 (current on Arch), Linux HID and systemd sources. Isolated runs with stubbed `hyprctl` and `omarchy-osd`, the real or a stubbed `omarchy-hw-touchpad`, and a private home: the repository test on the current and earlier heads, a mode-only restore, mutants of the new `enable()` logic, and probes for stale, duplicate, empty and special-character saved names (no other issues found). The dev-link case used a stand-in copy on PATH, not a linked install. No live compositor or input hardware was used.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
